positioning: A portfolio of public-safe financial AI evaluation assets, anchored by runnable financial agent evaluation.

tracks.title: Add the first public-source financial search task
tracks.why_it_matters: Search is the first tool-use step in many financial agents; wrong-source failures are easy to understand and easy to share.
acceptance_criteria: Add a task spec for public-source search.
Add a synthetic or public-safe fixture with at least three candidate sources.
Add a deterministic verifier that checks selected source, source type, period, and citation evidence.
Add one passing answer and one known-bad answer.
Include the task in the local runner and CI.

tracks.title: Build a finance RAG citation verifier
tracks.why_it_matters: Finance RAG systems often cite plausible but unsupported evidence; citation support is a concrete, reusable quality gate.
acceptance_criteria: Define a structured answer schema with citations, section IDs, and support notes.
Add a verifier that fails unsupported citations.
Add a known-bad answer with citation theater.
Add a stable Markdown report showing pass and fail behavior.

tracks.title: Generate a financial data-governance summary report
tracks.why_it_matters: Data leads need visible evidence that public sources, synthetic fixtures, and redistribution boundaries are controlled.
acceptance_criteria: Read source-manifest.json.
Summarize source IDs, packaging policies, review dates, allowed task families, and citation fields.
Fail validation if any task references an ungoverned source.
Write a stable Markdown report.

tracks.title: Add synthetic fixture authoring checks
tracks.why_it_matters: Synthetic examples are useful only when they are clearly labeled, inspectable, limited, and not framed as market evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Check fixture files for explicit synthetic labeling or dataset-card coverage.
Check expected answers for limitations and non-advice boundary.
Fail if production-readiness or investment recommendation language appears in reference answers.
Add CI coverage.

tracks.title: Publish a finance preference-review rubric schema
tracks.why_it_matters: Preference data in finance can reward confident but unsupported answers; a multi-axis rubric is more useful than a single winner label.
acceptance_criteria: Define JSON fields for evidence grounding, numeric correctness, safety boundary, citation support, and reviewer notes.
Add one passing and one failing sample review.
Add a lightweight schema validator.
Document adjudication triggers.

tracks.title: Write the public launch note for the multi-track strategy
tracks.why_it_matters: The project needs a crisp shareable narrative before outreach; the note should explain the gap without overclaiming.
acceptance_criteria: Explain why static finance QA is not enough for agent evaluation.
Link the runnable seed, failure gallery, RAG playbook, and governance control plane.
Avoid leaderboard and production-readiness claims.
Include a short call for issue/PR contributions.

tracks.title: Publish a finance-agent evaluation task matrix
tracks.why_it_matters: A task matrix gives different audiences clear entry points instead of forcing every reader through one long README.
acceptance_criteria: Map finance-agent task families to required evidence and failure modes.
Connect implemented artifacts to each task family.
List the next task gaps that can become issues.

tracks.title: Draft a Harbor-style finance task-pack blueprint
tracks.why_it_matters: Harbor is a visible agent-evaluation framework; a finance-domain task-pack blueprint gives this project a concrete way to participate without pretending to be official.
acceptance_criteria: State that the blueprint is not an official Harbor adapter.
Define task-pack shape, required metadata, and finance-specific verifier checks.
Include an upstream-friendly contribution path.

tracks.title: Add a forecasting / pastcasting cutoff task
tracks.why_it_matters: Forecasting and pastcasting are high-interest financial-agent tasks, but they are only credible when future-data leakage is explicitly tested.
acceptance_criteria: Add a synthetic or public-safe fixture with pre-cutoff and post-cutoff fields.
Add a verifier that fails use of post-cutoff evidence.
Add one passing answer and one known-bad answer.
Include uncertainty and non-advice boundary checks.

tracks.title: Add a financial tool-use trace task
tracks.why_it_matters: Tool order, failed-call recovery, and observation linkage are exactly where trajectory-aware frameworks can show value beyond final-answer grading.
acceptance_criteria: Define a task that requires quote, filing, and fundamentals-style observations.
Add a synthetic trajectory fixture with linked tool calls and observations.
Add a verifier for required tool order, missing evidence, and prohibited tool calls.
Add repeated-trial reporting fields.

tracks.title: Add a public-safe financial risk calculation task
tracks.why_it_matters: Risk calculations such as drawdown and volatility are common finance-agent workflows and are easier to verify deterministically than open-ended market commentary.
acceptance_criteria: Add a synthetic return or price fixture.
Add deterministic drawdown and volatility checks.
Add one passing answer and one known-bad answer.
Include unit, window, and non-advice boundary checks.

tracks.title: Add a portfolio-analysis boundary refusal task
tracks.why_it_matters: Personalized portfolio requests are a realistic regulated-domain boundary; the task can test whether an agent offers general education without collecting private account data or giving advice.
acceptance_criteria: Add an unsafe personalized portfolio request fixture.
Add a verifier for refusal, safe educational alternative, and no private-data request.
Add one passing answer and one known-bad answer.
Include non-advice and no-customer-data checks.

tracks.title: Add a benchmark-card validator and generated card
tracks.why_it_matters: A benchmark card turns the runnable seed into a more shareable evaluation artifact with visible provenance, leakage controls, intended use, and limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Add a benchmark-card YAML file for the financial-agent eval seed.
Add a validator that checks required provenance, leakage, safety, and report fields.
Link the benchmark card from the README and project pages index.
Include the validator in local verification and CI.

tracks.title: Add repeated-trial reporting for the financial-agent eval seed
tracks.why_it_matters: Repeated-trial reporting makes instability, missing evidence, and unsafe behavior visible beyond a single lucky pass.
acceptance_criteria: Add a small report aggregator for multiple run_finance_eval.py outputs.
Report pass rate, pass@k, Pass^k, missing-evidence rate, and unsafe-output rate where applicable.
Add a stable repeated-trial example report.
Document the workflow without ranking models or claiming production readiness.

tracks.title: Add a Harbor-style task-pack export manifest
tracks.why_it_matters: A task-pack manifest makes the 10 finance tasks easier for agent-framework maintainers to inspect, adapt, or discuss upstream.
acceptance_criteria: List all current Harbor-style tasks with fixture, solution, verifier, task metadata, source refs, and safety boundary.
Add a validator that fails if any task directory is missing required files or metadata.
Link the manifest from the Harbor finance blueprint and seed README.
State clearly that this is a public-safe example, not an official Harbor adapter.

tracks.title: Prepare a Harbor upstream discussion brief
tracks.why_it_matters: A concise upstream-friendly brief makes it easier to ask Harbor maintainers whether this belongs as docs, an example task pack, or an external reference.
acceptance_criteria: Summarize the public-safe finance task pack without claiming official support.
Link the task-pack manifest, benchmark card, repeated-trial report, and verifier commands.
Ask a specific maintainer-friendly question about the preferred contribution path.
Avoid promotional language, adoption claims, and private-domain examples.
